chapter: Stranded on the road and John Kirby
title: Milwaukee and the free tray of whiskey
summary: Kirby's band packed a Milwaukee bar owned by an old man's sons, where the band drank free and the boss turned his back at a rehearsal of bottles.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Then they brought in a fellow named Nelson, Kirby's man. Oh, Nelson. I forgot all about Nelson. He was in Kirby's band; he was a trumpet player. And we had a return engagement to Milwaukee -- a return engagement. We had been to Milwaukee, and put Milwaukee on the map, and did terrific business in a place that never had but three or four beer

drinkers a night... A great, big long bar, and they had about three customers a night in there drinking beer. And the man turned the place over to his two sons who had just come out of the Army. So the sons wanted to put music in the place, make it like a cabaret, put tables in there, it had this long bar and had the band behind the bar.

So they contacted Kirby, and Kirby had taken the band out to Milwaukee, and we opened up. Well, they had the band that I named before... No, it had Pete Clark, Wallace Bishop, Billy Kyle, Kirby, and who else....

Trumpet was Rostelle Reese. So anyway, they are trying something out with this band. Well, they had billed Kirby like a circus around there, on the air with his records and this-that-and-the-other, and consequently, the place was packed and jammed with people. Packed! Well, ...(?)... two kids in the country, man. I mean, one of them was 23 years old, the other was 25 -- nothing but kids. Because the old man had run the bar and never had over three customers in it, but he was a wealthy man. He was retiring, you know. And he was satisfied with the three customers.
But here's the kids up there, the place is packed full of people. They don't know what to do. They've got this big bar, and they've got a big tray on the end of the bar,
and it's all filled up with whiskey where the waitresses could come up and just take their glasses off, you know, for the orders and things. Big tray.

Well, when the band come off the bandstand, there was a place for us to sit down there if we wanted to sit. We don't know nothin' about Milwaukee. So we come off the stand and we're sittin' down there, and the guys are sittin' there talking, always BS'ing and one thing and another. And here's this big tray of whiskey sittin' up there on the edge of the bar. Oh, them cats wanted a drink so bad, and they see this whiskey lookin' them in the face, you can't help but smell it every time you walk by it. So we keep looking at it, looking for about two sets. So nothing happened.

Pretty soon, the third set, we're sittin' down there, and Bishop said, "I'm gonna get me one of them glasses of whiskey. I ain't gonna look at that whiskey no longer." He went up there and picked up a glass, picked this glass up and lifted it up, and looked around -- and there's the boss lookin' him right in the face, the old man. Bishop said, "This is on you." So the boss says, "Sure, sure, help yourself. Help yourself. After all, we're off the nut." He's made his money already. He said, "We're off the nut. Help yourself. Anything you see you want, help yourself."
He just shouldn't have said that. That's the worst

thing he could have said. All them cats scrambled for that tray. And then, when you go back on the stand, you had to pass through the bar. Well, there the bartenders all up there, everybody knew the bartenders, and the bartenders are right at your feet. So Pete is sitting next to me, and we had two bartenders sitting there -- our boys. And they would fix drinks, drinks, drinks, and they wasn't charging us... Nobody was charging anything. We could drink-drink-drink 'til it run out your ears. And we didn't have to pay a nickel for anything.

And Kirby even called a rehearsal. Now, to show you how square they were in this town, when the bar closed, the bartenders didn't even take the whiskey off the bar. Just leave it, you know, on the bar, right in the bottles and everything. And we come in to rehearse, and the bar was all set up! Heh-heh. So it's nobody there but us. And we're supposed to be rehearsing, and everybody got a bottle in his hand -- and in walks the boss. So he looked up there and seen everybody with a bottle... And he was so nice, you know what he did? He turned his back and went out the door. He didn't say a word. They was nice people. They was nice.
